advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile `_repair_plan`'s union-of-all-snapshots orphan classification with the single-anchor `is_snapshot_orphan` so scan, fold, and repair routing use one definition.
evidence: fsck_repair.py:228 `if name < latest_snap and file_uuid not in all_sources:` where `all_sources` is the union built at lines 208-217 over `for snap in snaps`
is_snapshot_orphan uses a single-snapshot anchor: `name < snapshot_filename and event_uuid not in source_uuids` (fsck_repair.py:79-84)
_check_snapshot calls the shared helper per-snapshot with that snapshot's own source_uuid_set (fsck_scan.py:381), while repair routing uses the union-based _repair_plan (fsck_repair.py:619)
advisory.finding: The shared `is_snapshot_orphan` predicate anchors to a SINGLE snapshot's `source_event_uuids`, but `_repair_plan` (which drives the new `fsck --repair-snapshots` triage routing) classifies orphans against the UNION of ALL snapshots' sources and the LATEST active snapshot. When a ticket has more than one active snapshot these two predicates can disagree about what is an orphan, undermining the commit's stated 'scan and fold can never disagree' invariant and the routing parity it adds.
scenarios: A ticket that has two active SNAPSHOT files (e.g. an inconsistent/uncompacted intermediate state) where an event is cited by an earlier snapshot but not the latest anchor

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Treat an unreadable/undecodable anchor snapshot in `_exclude_snapshot_orphans` as fail-closed (defer the fold) rather than excluding nothing and proceeding to retire+cite.
evidence: compact_txn.py:275-279 `try: with open(anchor,...) ... except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError): return old`
Returning `old` unchanged means the subsequent fold retires+cites every event including any true orphan (compact_txn.py:580 `fold_files = [fp for (fp,_u,_ts) in old]`)
Docstring claims symmetry with fsck but fsck only omits a finding, whereas the fold here performs an irreversible retire+cite
advisory.finding: `_exclude_snapshot_orphans` opens the anchor snapshot with a bare `open(anchor)` and on any `OSError`/`JSONDecodeError` returns `old` unchanged (excludes nothing), which means a transiently-unreadable or truncated anchor snapshot silently disables the anti-laundering guard for that fold — the exact failure mode the change exists to prevent. The docstring justifies this as symmetric with fsck, but fsck's `_check_snapshot` skipping an unreadable snapshot only suppresses a finding; here it re-enables destructive retirement+citation of a real orphan.
scenarios: A concurrently-written or partially-synced anchor snapshot that is briefly unreadable/truncated during the locked fold

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for `fsck --repair-snapshots --dry-run` on a HUMAN_TRIAGE orphan asserting the preview does not offer to rebuild (routing parity under dry-run).
evidence: fsck_repair.py:610-611 `if dry_run: return _dry_run_plan(...), findings` returns before the triage guard
fsck_repair.py:619-625 triage check runs only after the dry_run return
_dry_run_plan (fsck_repair.py:640-654) emits 'DRY-RUN: would rebuild SNAPSHOT' with no triage awareness
ABSENCE: no test in test_fold_orphan_laundering.py invokes fsck_cli with both --repair-snapshots and --dry-run; all triage tests call --repair-snapshots without --dry-run
advisory.finding: The dry-run branch of _repair_snapshots_ticket returns before the new triage-routing check, so `fsck --repair-snapshots --dry-run` against an order-sensitive (HUMAN_TRIAGE) orphan is not covered by any test; the dry-run preview would report 'would rebuild' instead of the TRIAGE routing the change introduces, and no regression test guards this.
scenarios: A user previews `fsck --repair-snapshots --dry-run` on a ticket with a STATUS orphan and is told it would rebuild, though the real run refuses (routing-parity divergence between preview and action)

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test corrupting the anchor SNAPSHOT's JSON and asserting _exclude_snapshot_orphans/the fold excludes nothing (no crash).
evidence: docstring claims 'An unreadable anchor snapshot excludes nothing — fsck cannot classify orphans against it either'
ABSENCE: no test writes a malformed anchor snapshot before folding to exercise the except branch
advisory.finding: The _exclude_snapshot_orphans unreadable-anchor fallback (excludes nothing on JSONDecodeError/OSError reading the anchor snapshot) is a new error path with no test corrupting or removing-read-permission on the anchor snapshot.
scenarios: A fold runs against a corrupt/unreadable prior SNAPSHOT; the code silently folds everything (excludes nothing) — behavior is documented but unverified
